title: F3: the family head with ATT&CK definitions as training rows and a margin against the closest rival family
question: Do ATT&CK's own technique definitions as training rows plus a loss term that makes the gold family beat its strongest rival by a margin reduce F2's look-alike confusions and raise family top-1?
motivation: F2's dev errors (260): the gold family was 2nd in 38%, the top-2 gap below 0.3 in 147; most frequent confusions Phishing for Information/Phishing, Data Encrypted for Impact/Archive Collected Data, Deobfuscate/Obfuscate, Command and Scripting Interpreter/Ingress Tool Transfer, OS Credential Dumping/Credentials from Password Stores

changes_from_f2.definitions: one row per listed technique, 'Name: description' (cleaned, cut at a sentence end within 1,500 characters), labelled with the technique (its family is the target); the same overlap filter against every dev and test set: 697 texts, 4 dropped (shared 10-token run), 693 kept, 221 families
changes_from_f2.margin: loss per example = cross-entropy over the gold families + 1.0 * max(0, 1.0 - (log P(gold families) - log P(strongest non-gold family))); lambda 1 and m 1 nats fixed, not tuned

fixed: as F2 otherwise: Cribl adapter + fresh head, F2's 24,034 rows + 693 definition rows = 24,727 rows, 2 epochs, checkpoint every quarter epoch, LoRA lr 1e-4, head lr 1e-3, 16 per step and per forward pass, seed 7; RunPod RTX 4090, CTI-HAL scored on the laptop
selection: as F1/F2: highest mean family top-1 over public dev and AnnoCTR dev; ties the earlier

success.headline: CTI-HAL family top-1: F3 minus F2 (same 968 statements), paired 95% CI lower bound above 0
secondary: AnnoCTR test family top-1: F3 minus F2, CI lower bound above 0
public test family top-1: F3 minus F2, CI lower bound above 0
success.reported: family micro-F1 top-1 and up to 3 families (threshold 0.25, not re-tuned); family top-1 on the look-alike subset = cases whose gold family is one of T1598, T1566, T1486, T1560, T1140, T1027, T1059, T1105, T1003, T1555 (fixed from F2's dev confusions before training); ECE; every checkpoint's dev curve

stop_rules: more than 1% of a split's cases end in error
confirmation_runs: the selected checkpoint once on CTI-HAL, public test and AnnoCTR test; nothing is chosen, refit or rerun because of a confirmation result
adoption: none: an experiment, no product wiring
informed_by: F2's dev predictions and error analysis, F2's confirmation results (docs 21.3.18), a laptop pilot (100 train rows, 30 dev cases; mechanics only). No F3 model exists.

amendments.change: compute is a RunPod secure RTX A6000 (48 GB, $0.59/h) instead of an RTX 4090
amendments.reason: no secure or community RTX 4090 was free
amendments.deviation: GPU floating-point differences against F2 (RTX 4090); same code, data, seed and settings

amendments.change: the first F3 run (RTX A6000, pod 7eosiv0hp8umf4) was stopped by RunPod at 19:19 UTC after 30,919 of 49,454 training examples (5 of 8 checkpoints); it is discarded and F3 is retrained from scratch on a RunPod secure RTX 4090, the GPU of the original registration and of F2
amendments.reason: the pod was stopped by the platform, not by the experiment; a mid-run resume would lose the optimiser state
amendments.deviation: none against the original registration (amendment 1's GPU change no longer applies); the discarded run's dev scores (checkpoints 0 to 30,919) were seen and are reported as such, nothing was chosen from them
amendments.informed_by: the discarded run's dev curve only (no test or CTI-HAL score exists)
